I have been farming these lands in Quzhou for 35 years, and at 65 I know what works. My household has five people, so we have the hands to manage labor-intensive crops. With 16.1 mu and a reliable well, I divide my land so the wheat-maize rotation anchors my food security and income, while cotton and garlic bring in extra cash.

This year I will keep **10.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation**. Wheat is my winter crop—I sowed it last October, and now in spring I need to topdress it and irrigate it well. I always rotary till before wheat and use improved seed. I expect about 500 kg per mu if I irrigate four times and spray pesticides four times. After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the stubble with no-tillage—this saves time and fuel, and the hybrids yield about 550 kg per mu. Maize only needs two irrigations and three pesticide sprays.

I am planting **3 mu of cotton** this summer. Cotton is tedious because the bollworm never sleeps, so I will spray 16 times through the season. I rotary till the cotton field in spring and use improved seed. With two irrigations and reasonable fertilizer, I should get about 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I also have **2.6 mu of garlic** that I planted last autumn. Garlic is a winter crop that overwinters in the field. I will irrigate it four times and spray twice for disease. I use improved cloves as seed, and if the spring is good I expect around 1,500 kg per mu. I will harvest it in late May, which also gives me time to prepare for the maize planting.

I do not chase new fads. The fertilizer rates I use are what I have learned from my neighbors and my own plots over the decades: wheat gets about 18 kg nitrogen, 11 kg phosphorus, and 4.5 kg potassium per mu; maize gets 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium; cotton gets 8 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 7.5 kg potassium; garlic is heavy-feeding, so I give it 21 kg nitrogen, 13 kg phosphorus, and 20 kg potassium.
